title: Spatiotemporal Profiling of RNA in Human Cell Lines Using SLAM-RT&Tag
author: Khyzha, Ahmad, et al.

steps.title: Collect and pellet K562 cells
steps.instruction: Collect 4 × 10⁶ K562 cells per reaction in a 15 mL Falcon tube, then centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 min at room temperature (22 °C) and discard the media.

steps.title: Wash cells with RNase‑inhibited buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL ice‑cold Wash Buffer containing RNase inhibitor at a 1:40 dilution using a 1 mL wide‑bore pipette tip; centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 min at 22 °C, carefully remove the supernatant, then resuspend the pellet in 500 µL NE1 buffer with RNase inhibitor (1:40) using a 1 mL wide‑bore tip.

steps.title: Lyse cells to release nuclei
steps.instruction: Incubate the suspension on ice for 10 min to lyse cells, centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 min at 22 °C, and carefully remove the supernatant (the nuclei pellet will be transparent and difficult to see).

steps.title: Wash isolated nuclei
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclei pellet in 1 mL Wash Buffer supplemented with RNase inhibitor (1:40) using a 1 mL wide‑bore tip; ensure all buffers also contain spermidine as required for nuclear speckle integrity.

steps.title: Bind nuclei to ConA beads
steps.instruction: Distribute 50 µL of the resuspended nuclei (≈200 000 nuclei) into each PCR tube that already contains 5 µL pre‑activated ConA beads, using a 200 µL wide‑bore tip; mix gently by pipetting up and down and incubate at room temperature (22 °C) for 10 min to allow nuclei to bind to the beads.

steps.title: Prepare Tapestation samples
steps.instruction: Combine 2 µL of each library sample with 2 µL of sample dye in PCR strip tubes; also prepare a ladder tube with 2 µL ladder + 2 µL dye. Vortex each tube thoroughly and spin briefly to collect liquid.

steps.title: Run Tapestation and assess library size
steps.instruction: Run the High Sensitivity D5000 Tapestation chip according to the manufacturer’s instructions; verify that library fragments range from 200–700 bp. If a prominent ~150 bp peak (adapter artifact) is observed, perform an additional AMPure XP bead cleanup before re‑running.

description: We previously developed Reverse Transcribe & Tagment (RT&Tag),2 a proximity labeling method that leverages antibody-mediated enzyme tethering to capture RNAs in spatial proximity of an epitope. While RT&Tag maps the steady-state RNA populations of nuclear compartments, it does not provide information on RNA turnover. To overcome this limitation, we established SLAM-RT&Tag, which integrates principles of RNA metabolic labeling from SLAM-seq3 with RT&Tag to enable spatiotemporal profiling of compartment-associated transcripts. This protocol describes the application of SLAM-RT&Tag to profile the RNA dynamics within nuclear speckles in human K562 cells. Nuclear speckles are nuclear compartments enriched in polyadenylated RNA and RNA processing factors, which we targeted due to their implication in post-transcriptional splicing.1,4 K562 cells are pulsed with 4-thiouridine (s4U) to label nascent RNAs. K562 nuclei are then isolated and bound to paramagnetic beads. The nuclear speckle transcriptome is then captured using an antibody (SC35) targeting the speckle-associated protein, SRRM2.5 Biotinylated oligo(dT) and pAG-Tn5 are then tethered, followed by targeted reverse transcription and tagmentation. The s4U nucleotides are then misread by the reverse transcriptase, leading to the incorporation of G instead of A in the cDNA strand. This step results in T-to-C mutations when generating Illumina sequencing libraries by PCR amplification. Illumina sequencing libraries are then sequenced and T-to-C conversion events are computationally deduced to quantify half-lives. While this protocol is demonstrated in K562 cells, it is adaptable to other cell types and nuclear compartments, provided sufficient s4U labeling efficiency and nuclei input. The success of SLAM-RT&Tag relies on the use of high-quality, validated antibodies. An IgG antibody should be included as a control to account for global half-lives and serve as a measure of input for the assay. Incorporation of s4U is used
